chapters.title: What Get It? is
chapters.text:
Some lessons land. Some do not - and you often find out weeks later, from the children who never put their hand up.
Asking in front of the class does not work. They are the last to admit it.
Marking the books does not tell you either. A right answer can be copied.
Get It asks each pupil properly - one to one, in their own words.
And it shows you the gaps while you can still fix them.

chapters.title: Create your account
chapters.text:
Start by making an account. Email, password, that is it.
No card. No countdown.
Your classes are saved to the account, so they follow you to any computer in the school.
Nothing to install. Nothing for IT to set up. And no new system for anyone else to learn.
It is a teaching aid, so it will not ask you for anything you are not already doing.
Once you are in, you are ready for your first check.

chapters.title: Set up your class
chapters.text:
Give the class a name, and Get It gives you a join code.
That code never changes. Pin it up on the wall and use it all year. There is a QR code too, if they are on tablets.
Now paste your class list, straight from SIMS or Arbor. One name per line. You only do this once.
From then on, every pupil picks their own name from the list. No typing. No spelling mistakes. And nobody slipping in as somebody else.
They can do it on a laptop, a tablet, or a phone.

chapters.title: Put the code on the wall
chapters.text:
Your class has one code, and it does not change.
Copy the code into a message, or into the homework post.
Or copy the link, and it takes them straight to the right page with nothing to type.
Show the QR code on the board and they scan it with a tablet or a phone.
Print it and pin it up, so it is already there next lesson and you have done nothing.
Whichever you use, it is the same code all year, and every class keeps its own. You never set this up twice.

chapters.title: Tell it the year group
chapters.sub: So the marking expects the right amount
chapters.text:
When you make a class, you can say which year it is.
That only tells the marking how much explaining to expect. A Year 7 answer and a Year 11 answer are not the same answer.
It does not change the questions, and it does not change the marks.
Leave it as not set and nothing changes at all.

chapters.title: Write the questions
chapters.sub: You type the topic. That is it.
chapters.text:
Now the bit that used to take your Sunday evening.
Type what you just taught. Press generate, and the questions are written for you.
Then read them properly. Rewrite one if you do not like the wording. Delete any you would not ask in class. Add your own if you have a better one.
It takes seconds, and nothing is set in stone.
The questions are the check, so make them yours.
Then press create check. It is live for that class, waiting until they are ready.
Next lesson, do the same again. Every check stays in the list, so nothing gets lost.

chapters.title: How pupils join
chapters.sub: Play this one on the whiteboard
chapters.text:
This is the one to play on the whiteboard.
Pupils open the link, put in the code, and pick their name from your list. There are no accounts and no logins for them.
They tick one box: that their answers go to you, and to an AI that helps you read them. That box explains itself, and there is a privacy page if anyone wants the detail.
Then the interesting part.
It does not give them a quiz to tick boxes on. A tick tells you nothing.
It asks them to explain it, in their own words. Then it reads that answer and digs deeper. Asking why. Asking what happens if.
It keeps going until it finds real understanding, or finds the gap.
When it is done, it thanks them. Their answers come straight to you. They never see a mark.

chapters.title: What the pupil sees
chapters.text:
It is worth seeing this from their side once.
They pick their name, tick the box, and start.
It does not give them a quiz to tick. It asks them to explain it, and then it asks again - why, and what if.
If they have learned it off by heart, that shows. If they have understood it, that shows too.
It keeps going until it is sure, then thanks them and sends their answers to you.
They never see a mark, so nobody has to be wrong in front of the class.

chapters.title: Read your results
chapters.sub: Who got it, who did not
chapters.text:
Back on the teacher tab, open the check.
Here is the whole class in one look. Green got it. Amber is shaky. Red did not get it yet.
You did not mark any of this. You did not read thirty sets of answers to find the three that matter.
Under each pupil is the evidence. Every point they were meant to show, and their own words beside it. So you can check the claim yourself instead of taking its word for it.
Click a name and the card folds down to one line, which is handy when you are looking at the whole class.
And it says so on the screen: this is guidance, not a grade. The judgement is yours.

chapters.title: Change a colour yourself
chapters.text:
The AI reads answers. Sometimes it reads them wrong.
So you can change any colour, by hand.
Say it called a pupil red, and you know she is part way there. Click amber. That is her colour now, and it is the one that counts. The AI's own read stays beside it, so you can see where you disagreed.
Your change is remembered, so it does not flip back next lesson.

chapters.title: Spot the pattern
chapters.text:
Go back to the class.
Every pupil has a line of dots, and every check adds one more.
One red is a bad day. Two of those together is a pattern, and you can see it in about three seconds. Not three weeks later, on the drive home.
Anyone who has finished is greyed out, so you can see who you are still waiting on.
You are not guessing who is struggling any more. You are looking at it, while you can still do something about it.

chapters.title: Take the record away
chapters.sub: A pupil, or the whole class
chapters.text:
Sometimes you need it somewhere other than the screen.
Open a pupil and you get every check they have done in this class, in one place. What they got, what was shaky, and their own words underneath.
That is what you read before a parents' evening. So you are not reading thirty answers to find the three that matter.
Export results and the whole class comes out as a spreadsheet. Every check, every pupil, the colour and the reason for it.
It is your data, in a form you can hand to somebody else.

chapters.title: Your data, and theirs
chapters.text:
A word about data, because it matters.
There is a privacy page in plain English. What is kept. Who sees it. What is not done with it. No ads, no tracking, nothing sold.
Your school's policy comes first. If it does not allow pupil answers to go to an outside service, do not use it for that.
You can export a class as a spreadsheet. You can delete a check, with every answer in it. Or delete a class and everything under it.
Last thing. This is a teaching aid, not an assessment. The AI can be wrong. Your judgement is the one that counts.

chapters.title: If it gets it wrong
chapters.sub: Tell me, and it gets better
chapters.text:
One more thing, and it matters if you are going to trust this.
It reads answers, and sometimes it reads one badly. You will spot it, because you know the child.
When that happens, there is a link at the bottom of the page. Tell me what happened, and what you expected instead.
That is how the marking improves, and it is the honest position. The judgement is yours.
